Asset-class outlook · November 2026 to October 2027

The size of the swings can be forecast. The gains cannot.

Each month this model looks 12 asset classes a year ahead: what each has earned above cash on average, how wide the range of outcomes is, and how much of that deserves belief. Market data through 30 October 2026.

How far to trust it

The risk side is tested. The return side is an average.

  • Tested

    How bumpy each asset will be

    Scored once on 2014–2025 forecasts the model had never seen, its forecast error was 7.8% lower than a simple benchmark's.

  • Unproven

    How assets move together

    On 2014–2025 forecasts the model had never seen, it finished 1.2% ahead of a simple benchmark, a gap chance alone could produce.

  • Average only

    How much each asset will earn

    A long-run average since 1926, not a prediction. 6 forecasting models were tested against it and none did reliably better. For 6 of the 12 assets the data cannot rule out an average of zero above cash.

  • Not predicted

    When a crisis starts

    The forecast follows the general level of risk and reacts only after a shock, as 2008–⁠09 and 2020 show below.

What it means for borrowing

Borrowing buys more doubt than gain

5.25%Robinhood margin rate, balances up to $50,000
3.9%what cash earns (T-bills)
1.4%yearly cost of each borrowed dollar above cash

Read the curve as arithmetic, not as a tested strategy. At the same risk as each sample portfolio the best mix is ahead by 0.6 to 1.1 points a year, and for all of them the plausible range includes zero. In back-tests, portfolios chosen by an optimizer swung 19% more than forecast. The report’s rule: add about 22% to the forecast swing of any optimized or borrowed portfolio.

How the forecast is made

Many models for risk, one long average for return

  1. 1871

    Market history

    Prices for 12 asset classes; the oldest series starts in 1871.

  2. 70

    Risk models compared

    Each estimates how bumpy every asset will be.

  3. 9

    Families averaged

    The models’ families are blended, so no single blind spot decides.

  4. 1926

    Average returns added

    Each asset’s average gain above cash over its recorded history.

  5. 12 mo

    A range for the year

    Risk and average combine into the ranges above, every month.

Gains are ordinary yearly percentages above cash (T-bills). The full report states the same forecast as compounded returns, so its figures read lower. Ranges are built from how these assets have behaved in the past; crises are not anticipated. Forecasts made from November 2026 on are the first that can count as new evidence for the return side; the first is judged in November 2027.

Planning inputs, not investment advice. Every figure is produced by code in the repository from the forecast dated 2026-10-31: see reports/REPORT.md and forecasts/latest.
